findings.title: Hardcoded outcome prices assume factory P0 near100
findings.trigger: Any valid injected factory with signal.reference_price>112/1.10; public F697 P0=114 is a concrete available counterexample.
findings.effect: The maximum high112 cannot prove +10% from114 (target125.4), so evaluateOutcome returns MISS for complete bars and the HIT assertion fails before projection/recovery witnesses. This is fixture portability, not a strategy defect.
findings.minimal_proposal: Let p=signal.reference_price; use open/close=p, low=p*0.99, nonhit high=p*1.05 and one hit high=p*1.12. Keep original t0/windows and actual evaluateOutcome. Alternatively explicitly require P0=100 in the factory contract; do not silently assume it.

findings.title: Two first READY denominators are reported without both journal-anchor assertions
findings.trigger: immutableKeys excludes both pump:journal raw rows; audit is called only with sent.summary/sent.later; returned raw_first_READY_denominators is constant2.
findings.effect: The case checks two recovery references and immutable originals, but does not directly prove that both native raw journals retain their first READY analysis/recorded_ts/frozen anchor. A firstREADY shift in the UNSENT journal is not explicitly witnessed by the asserted denominator count.
findings.minimal_proposal: Before guarded work capture each raw journal first READY analysis_id, origin.t0, recorded_ts and frozen_anchor; after yield/repair/unknown assert them against originals. If claiming denominator2, audit both SENT and terminal UNSENT summary records, or report only the actually checked reference count. No new runtime IO is needed; these are controlled inspection assertions.
